title: Atlas-3 sensor: product brief
paragraphs: The Atlas-3 is a battery-powered water-quality sensor. It sends readings every 15 minutes through the Telemetry Gateway.
The Atlas-3 main board uses the QX-7 radio chip for its cellular link. The housing is the IP68 enclosure, which is rated for continuous immersion to two metres.
The Atlas-3 runs on one LX-4 lithium cell. Battery life is rated at five years at the default reading interval.
Atlas-3 units are assembled at the Tartu plant.

title: Borealis controller: release notes 2.4
paragraphs: Borealis 2.4 adds Modbus support. The Borealis controller now takes power from the PM-2 power module, which replaces the older PM-1.

title: Meridian flow meter: launch note
paragraphs: The Meridian flow meter is our new product for irrigation networks. It reports flow and pressure every five minutes through TGW, our telemetry gateway.
Meridian uses the same QX7 modem as the Atlas-3 for its cellular link. Its flow element is the FS-9 sensing element, supplied by Kerrin Sensors.
Meridian units are assembled at the Tartu plant, on the line next to the Atlas-3.

title: Incident review: QX-7 shipment delay
paragraphs: On 3 March 2026, Varnell Semiconductor told us that QX-7 shipments would slip by six weeks because of a wafer shortage.
The review recommended qualifying a second radio-chip supplier by the end of Q3 and keeping eight weeks of chip stock on hand.
No customer shipments were missed, because the warehouse held enough finished units to cover the gap.

title: Engineering note: Atlas-3 battery change
paragraphs: From the May build, the Atlas-3 uses the Sundra C2 cell from Sundra Power instead of the LX-4 lithium cell.
We made the change because the LX-4 lost a third of its capacity below minus ten degrees in the Osterby winter trials, which would have cut battery life to under three years for northern customers.
The Sundra C2 has the same footprint, so the main board does not change.

title: Incident review: Telemetry Gateway outage
paragraphs: On 14 May 2026, the Telemetry Gateway rejected device connections for three hours. Every device that uploads through the gateway lost data for that window.
The cause was an expired TLS certificate on the gateway's load balancer. Uploads from Atlas-3 sensors, Borealis controllers and Meridian flow meters all failed.
The review recommended automating certificate renewal and alerting 30 days before any certificate expires.

title: Meeting notes: supply chain stand-up
paragraphs: Attendees: M. Feld (Supply Chain team lead), Tomas Berg, Priya Raman.
Main supply risks: the QX-7 is still mostly single-sourced until Kerrin volumes ramp, and Varnell also makes the PM-2, so a problem at Varnell would hit both the Atlas-3 and the Borealis at once.
The enclosure is low risk, since we own the tooling. The battery change removes our dependence on Hallam for the Atlas-3.
